record_title: Two-prime classification of exponential unitary perfect numbers
scientific_context: The only exponential unitary perfect integer with exactly two distinct prime factors is 36. The proof splits the two normalized exponential-unitary divisor sums into complementary pure powers and then uses a sharp ratio bound to reduce the exponent of 2 to 2 or 4. Consequently, any e-unitary perfect number that is not e-perfect must have at least three distinct prime factors.
limitations: The result classifies only one- and two-prime support and does not resolve whether every e-unitary perfect number is e-perfect. Originality is to the best of our knowledge; the main residual risk is an older result hidden under variant terminology. The 1971 Notices abstract was available through indexed text but its full issue was not directly inspected, and the 1978 e-perfect paper was checked for its relevant two-prime conclusion through a standard handbook summary. The finite verification supports but does not replace the proof; no formal proof-assistant verification or independent audit is asserted.

artifact_inventory.description: Standalone exact-integer implementation of exponential-unitary divisor sums, a bounded search for two-prime examples, and a check of the exponent bound.
Deterministic output of the finite verification.
